features.description: tests/run.sh becomes a runner over tests/checks/NN-<slug>.sh files cut from the monolith by its `# ---- <title> ----` markers through tests/split.sh, with tests/lib.sh as the shared preamble and a conformance check proving every one of the 325 check names survived (suite-split spec S1).
steps: tests/lib.sh has a one-line usage header; `suite_setup` is the pre-split tests/run.sh lines 6-58 made a function (temp dir, private tmux socket, the exported stub environment, the base user config, the throwaway project with its bare origin) and the helpers check/hlog/list/on_main/curl_with/curl_body/curl_last/curl_count/win/wins/in_has/desk_of are unchanged; `suite_end` prints `N/M checks passed` for the file and exits 1 on a failure; HERE is tests/

tests/split.sh (kept in the repo, run once against the pre-split monolith at the commit before the split) writes tests/checks/NN-<slug>.sh in file order, each `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib.sh" && suite_setup`, the section's lines byte for byte, `suite_end`; its grouping pairs (`title -> title`, a section that fails alone but passes in the monolith is grouped with the section it reads from, never patched) are listed at its top with one line each on why
the sorted multiset of `check "..."` lines across tests/checks/*.sh equals the monolith's (diff empty): no check line was edited

tests/run.sh is the runner: no arguments runs every tests/checks/*.sh; arguments run the files whose names match any of them (`bash tests/run.sh parked` runs only the parked file and ends with that file's count); it prints each file's PASS/FAIL lines and ends with the total `N/M checks passed`, exit 1 on any failure; `KEEP=1 bash tests/run.sh gc` keeps that file's $T and prints its path

tests/fixtures/check-names.txt is the sorted list of the 325 check names of the single-file suite, generated from the monolith's output (this run's init left it at /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-10-26/check.out; else run the monolith at the pre-split commit), never hand-typed; the runner's own check `conformance: the split suite has every check the single-file suite had` fails on a missing or duplicated name and prints the names that are new when they are not in the fixture

every tests/checks/*.sh passes alone from a fresh shell (`for f in tests/checks/*.sh; do bash "$f" | tail -1; done` prints only `N/N checks passed` lines); `bash -n` passes on tests/lib.sh, tests/split.sh, tests/run.sh and every tests/checks/*.sh
`bash tests/run.sh` ends `N/N checks passed` with N = 325 + the conformance check, and lib/check.sh (CHECK_CMD="bash tests/run.sh") still reports it green with its test count

features.description: The runner runs the check files TEST_JOBS at a time as plain background jobs inside the one check scope, replays each file's output whole, prints a timing line per file and the slowest three, and the full suite takes under 150 s on this box (suite-split spec S2).
steps: tests/run.sh starts files TEST_JOBS at a time (default min(nproc/2, 4), at least 1) with `wait -n`, never through systemd-run; each file's output goes to $T/<file>.out and is printed whole in completion order, so PASS/FAIL lines of two files never interleave

one timing line per file `<file>: <n> checks, <s> s`, then a line naming the slowest three files and the wall time as the second-to-last line; the total `N/M checks passed` stays the last line (testcount.mjs reads it); a file that exits non-zero makes the runner exit 1 and name that file

a new check file by topic, tests/checks/NN-suite-runner.sh: the runner pointed at a scratch directory of three tiny check files (two green, one red; an env or argument the runner takes for its checks directory) with TEST_JOBS=1 and TEST_JOBS=4 gives the same N/M and the same sorted PASS names, exits 1, names the red file and prints the timing lines; its check names are added to tests/fixtures/check-names.txt

the parallel run itself makes no systemd-run call: a check runs the runner with a spy `systemd-run` first on PATH and sees no call from the runner (files that start harness runs log the harness's own session scopes, which is expected); with TEST_JOBS=1 and TEST_JOBS=4 the per-file check counts and the set of PASS names are the same

the wall time with TEST_JOBS=4 (`time bash tests/run.sh`) is measured and written with the slowest file, the per-file times, the floor (the slowest file, or the file time divided by the jobs) and the suite's peak memory (read from the run's check scope, `scope_peak`) into journal/decisions/2026-10-26-suite-split.md: 165 s on 2026-10-26 before the retro run's 50 checks, 203 s after them (slowest file 157 s); a performance number here is measured and recorded, not a gate (Michael, 2026-10-26)
CLAUDE.md § How to verify states the measured duration, TEST_JOBS, and the subset form by file name (`bash tests/run.sh gc`)
`bash -n` on tests/run.sh and every tests/checks/*.sh; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: CHECK_KEY_IGNORE leaves path prefixes the suite never reads out of the suite cache key, so a plan or decision file no longer forces a full pre-suite run (suite-split spec S3).
steps: lib/config.sh defaults CHECK_KEY_IGNORE=".harness/runs docs/plans"; this repo's .harness/config.sh sets CHECK_KEY_IGNORE=".harness/runs docs/plans docs/specs journal findings-and-research ledger"; templates/project/config.sh has the line commented with one sentence on what it does

lib/treekey.mjs reads HARNESS_CHECK_KEY_IGNORE (space-separated prefixes; `.harness/runs` alone when unset) and adds one `:!<prefix>` pathspec per entry; lib/driver.sh exports it beside HARNESS_CHECK_CMD so check.sh in sessions and in the driver see the same key; `node --check lib/treekey.mjs` passes

unit checks in a tests/checks file on the suite cache (the capped-suites file or a new NN-check-key.sh): two trees that differ only under an ignored prefix print the same 16-hex key; a change under lib/ changes it

lib/check.sh's cached line reads `check: green (cached for this code tree, N tests; key ignores: docs/plans ...)` only when the ignore list differs from the default, and the plain `check: green (cached for this code tree, N tests)` otherwise

a stub-run check: a run whose stub session adds only docs/plans/x.md gets a `check: green (cached` line before its next session, and one whose session edits a tracked file under lib/ does not; both names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt
docs/architecture.md §4 (the suite cache row) and README.md name CHECK_KEY_IGNORE and its default
`bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

it names the stub-claude flags the new checks need (a session that commits .harness/runs/x in the slot, one that writes a question above ## Answers, a delayed bookkeeping for the lock check) and says each copies a real shape (fakes mirror the live API)

features.description: The pure pieces: features.mjs gains `lanes` (the milestones that can open now), `next` with a milestone argument and `pass`; scope_owns accepts the `<m>-` role prefix; config.sh and the user template gain the lane defaults.
steps: `node lib/features.mjs lanes <list> <attempts> <max> <parked> <state dir>` prints in list order one `<m>\t<base tags>` line per milestone that has a feature left to try, is not verified-<m>, needs-<m> or open ($STATE/lanes/<m>/pid alive), and whose every dependency has verified-<dep> in the state dir; its dependencies are the milestones named by its first feature's `after` plus any milestone another feature's `after` points into; a first feature without `after` depends on every earlier milestone; features with no milestone form lane `default`, first

`next <list> <attempts> <max> <parked> [<m>]` restricted to <m> picks only that milestone's features, and a feature without `after` waits on the earlier features of its own milestone only; `pass <list> <id>` flips passes to true (the mirror of unpass)

tests/checks/NN-lanes-scheduler.sh has the five unit checks: an undeclared first feature waits on every earlier milestone; `after: []` opens at once; a feature's `after` into another milestone makes the lane wait for it; a needs-<m> milestone never opens; a feature with no `after` waits on its milestone's earlier features only; plus one for `pass`

lib/scope.sh's role regex is `^([A-Za-z0-9_]+-)?(s[0-9]+|check-[0-9]+|svc)$`: a check that scope_owns run harness-<run>-M1-s3.scope and harness-<run>-M1-check-42.scope and harness-<run>-M1-svc.scope, and rejects harness-<run>-M1-x.scope and harness-<run>-s3-extra.scope

lib/config.sh defaults MAX_LANES=1 LANE_RESERVE_GB=4 LANE_OPEN_BELOW_5H=70 LANE_REBASE=suite MAX_REBASE_ROUNDS=1 RECORD_PR=end, each with a short why; templates/user/config.sh has them commented; HARNESS_LANE_POLL (default 10, the suite sets 1) is documented in the driver's usage header
`node --check lib/features.mjs`, `bash -n lib/scope.sh lib/config.sh`; the new names are in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: The record travels on its own branch: the driver (still one loop) writes .harness/runs/<run>/ only on harness/<run> under the record lock, runs coding sessions in slot-0 on harness-lane/<run>/<m> with the record materialized and taken back, verifies on the lane tip and merges that tag; taint and held logic is gone and the record checks assert the record branch.
steps: the shared record library of the plan exists with the `record()` flock helper wrapping every record write, $STATE/sessions replaces the shell counter n (MAX_SESSIONS is checked against the file) and $STATE/limits replaces limits; a check: two background writers through the helper with a stub delay (an env the library honours only in tests) appending 20 lines each lose none (40 lines, every one intact)

slot open: `git worktree add` of $HARNESS_WORKTREES/<project>/lanes/<run>/slot-0 at origin/main on first use, `git checkout -B harness-lane/<run>/<m>` on reuse, then `git merge --no-edit run/<run>/<dep>` for every dependency whose tag is not an ancestor of origin/main; a conflict gives `note "<m>: its base conflicts (<dep> vs main); needs Michael"` and needs-<m>; `harness start --base <ref>` replaces origin/main for the record branch and every lane; prompt_vars renders the slot as WT; run_init, context, the coding session, check.sh and verify all run in the slot

materialization: before a session .harness/runs/<run>/ is copied into the slot with `git config extensions.worktreeConfig true` (once) and `git config --worktree core.excludesFile $STATE/lanes/<m>/exclude` holding `.harness/runs/`; after it, under the lock, entry.json is taken, `F repair` runs on the slot's list against the pre-session snapshot and the flip is applied to the record's list with `F pass`, the lines the session added above `## Answers` are appended to the record's INBOX.md via `notify.mjs question`, and the slot's copy is removed; a lane commit touching .harness/runs/ is reverted by a new commit with `note "<id>: a lane commit touched the run record; reverted"`

checks (tests/checks/NN-lanes-record.sh): a stub session that commits .harness/runs/x in the slot gets the revert note and harness/<run> is unchanged by it; a stub session that writes a question above ## Answers has it in the record's INBOX.md; two sessions' passes flips both land while the record moved between them

verify runs in the slot on the lane branch (origin/main merged in first, the verify session in the lane's scope, the evidence count, the escalation, green on that tree, tag run/<run>/<m> at the lane tip pushed) then merge_one; `grep -c 'tainted\|held' lib/driver.sh` is 0; a lane's PR is opened at verify and merged only when every dependency has merged-<dep>, else `note "<m> verified; its PR waits for <dep> to merge"` once; merge_milestones tries every verified unmerged milestone in list order and `harness merge <run>` calls it

the two invariant checks: after the demo run `git -C $T/origin.git diff --quiet run/demo/M2 main` (what lands on main is byte for byte what was verified) and no PR's diff in the stub gh's record touches a .harness/runs/ path while harness/demo holds every entry (entries.jsonl lines = sessions) and `git -C $T/origin.git ls-tree -r main --name-only | grep -c .harness/runs/` is 0

the record checks listed in the plan are rewritten to assert the record on harness/<run> and that no code PR touches .harness/runs/; every other check keeps its text (every name in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt still present); `bash -n` on every shell file touched; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: lib/lane.sh runs one milestone as its own process (features, then verify and merge, exit codes 0/10-15) and lib/driver.sh becomes the coordinator that opens lanes under MAX_LANES=1 every HARNESS_LANE_POLL seconds, reaps them, computes the end reason and finishes with every slot removed.
steps: lib/lane.sh <m> has a usage header, sources config.sh, prompt.sh, scope.sh, notify.sh and the record library, takes LANE, LANE_SLOT, LANE_PORT from its environment, and loops: control (pause: wait between sessions; stop: exit 14), limit_wait, the weekly gate, `F next ... <m>`, run_init in harness-<run>-<m>-svc on the lane's port, materialize, context, the clock line, the coding session in harness-<run>-<m>-s<n> (n from $STATE/sessions), the WIP commit, journal, the environmental branch (unbump, LIMIT_UNTIL), repair, the red-suite un-pass, metrics with `lane: "<m>"`, park; when `F milestone-done` holds it runs verify and merge_one and exits 0 (verified and merged, or proposed under pr), else 10 given up <id>, 11 parked <id>, 12 needs Michael, 13 limit ended, 14 stopped, 15 deadline; the reason is written to $STATE/lanes/<m>/exit; its EXIT trap runs services_down for the lane's scope

lib/driver.sh's loop is the coordinator: start-up as today (record worktree, INBOX, brief, deploy check, initializer in the record worktree, deps-noted); then every HARNESS_LANE_POLL seconds: control (pause: logged once, nothing opened; stop: nothing opened, wait for lanes, finish "stopped by Michael"), deadline, limit_wait, weekly_over, reap lanes whose pid is gone (`note "lane <m> closed (<why>)"`, slot freed), `F lanes`, admission `lanes alive < MAX_LANES`, open each with pid/port/slot written and `note "lane <m> opened (slot <k>, port <n>, from <sha>)"`; with no lane alive and none opening the end reason is computed as today (done · blocked on <ids> · waiting on Michael: <ids> · no feature left to try); MAX_SESSIONS and MAX_LIMIT_HITS end the run from the coordinator when a lane's exit reports them

finish waits for every lane, removes every slot (`git worktree remove --force`), deletes the lane branches of merged milestones locally and on origin and keeps unverified ones; `git worktree list` afterwards shows one worktree for the run (the record's)

the stub run with MAX_LANES=1 and today's three-feature list ends `done` with M1 and M2 merged by two PRs, harness-log.md has `lane M1 opened (slot 0` before `lane M1 closed (` and the same for M2, every metrics.jsonl coding row carries `lane`, and harness/demo holds every entry

`harness pause` makes the lane finish its session and wait (no new session, `paused` logged once by the coordinator) and `harness stop` ends with every $STATE/lanes/*/pid dead and no lanes/ directory left under $HARNESS_WORKTREES/proj

the new checks live in tests/checks/NN-lanes-run.sh (or the rewritten run-1 file), names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `bash -n lib/lane.sh lib/driver.sh`; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: harness continue reopens lanes from their origin branches, refuses a legacy run (code commits on the run branch) with three ways forward, continues a record-only branch, and a verified lane whose dependency is pr-held opens from the dependency's tag with its PR opened and not merged.
steps: `harness continue <run>` reopens a lane whose branch origin/harness-lane/<run>/<m> exists by `checkout -B` from it instead of the base, attempts reset as today; a check: a run stopped mid-M2 and continued finishes M2 on the same lane branch with its earlier lane commits still in the merged PR

`harness continue` on a run whose branch has commits outside .harness/runs/ beyond origin/main prints the three options (`harness merge <run>` for its verified milestones; a new run with --brief naming the old branch as the source for what is left; finishing by hand) and exits 1; a run whose branch is record-only continues as a lanes run; one check each

under MERGE_POLICY=pr with M2 depending on M1: M1 verified is proposed (PR open, not merged, no merged-M1); M2 opens from origin/main with run/<run>/M1 merged in (`note "lane M2 opened (... from <sha>)"` where <sha> contains the tag), M2 verified opens its PR and `note "M2 verified; its PR waits for M1 to merge"` appears once; `harness merge <run>` afterwards merges both in order (the run 10 and run 14 checks keep their text and pass)

the new checks live in tests/checks/NN-lanes-continue.sh, names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; README.md says what `harness continue` tells a legacy run; `bash -n bin/harness lib/driver.sh lib/lane.sh`; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: The re-base rule: when main moved under a verified lane, disjoint files re-run the suite on the merged tree and re-tag, overlapping files get one verify round, LANE_REBASE=verify always verifies, and the merged tree is what lands on main.
steps: when merge_one finds the merge-tree of the tag onto origin/main differs from the tag's tree, the lane merges origin/main into its branch (a conflict is today's needs-Michael path); the files main brought in (`git diff --name-only <tag>..HEAD`) and the milestone's own (`git diff --name-only <base>..<tag>`) are compared; disjoint: the suite runs on the merged tree in the lane's check scope and, green, `git tag -f -a run/<run>/<m>` at the merged commit is pushed with `--force` to that tag ref only, `note "<m> re-based on <main>: <n> files, disjoint, suite green; re-tagged"`, then the merge; overlapping: one more verify round on the merged tree under MAX_REBASE_ROUNDS, then tag and merge, else needs Michael; LANE_REBASE=verify makes every case the verify round

checks in tests/checks/NN-lanes-rebase.sh: lane A merges a file B never touched while B is verifying -> B's note says disjoint, the stub log shows the suite ran, B is re-tagged and merged, and `git -C $T/origin.git diff --quiet run/<run>/B main` holds after B (the invariant); A touching a file B changed -> B gets a verify round, then merges; LANE_REBASE=verify -> the verify round in the disjoint case too; the force push appears in the git record only for refs/tags/run/<run>/B
under MERGE_POLICY=pr, `harness merge <run>` opens a slot from the tag and runs the same rule (a check with main moved between verify and merge)

journal/decisions/2026-10-26-lane-rebase-disjoint.md (title, provenance, finding · choice · rejected: always re-verify, never re-run, merge without a check); names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `bash -n` on the shell files touched; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: Slots are reused by checkout -B (ignored build directories survive across milestones), merged lane branches are deleted locally and on origin, and harness gc reaps lane branches, leftover slots and lane units of ended runs while leaving a live run alone.
steps: a lane opens in the lowest free slot; a slot's worktree is created once per run and reused by `git checkout -B`; a check: the second milestone opened in slot-0 still finds an ignored directory (e.g. node_modules/marker) the first left

when a lane's PR merges: `git branch -D harness-lane/<run>/<m>` and `git push origin --delete harness-lane/<run>/<m>`, the slot freed; under pr the slot is freed at verify and the branch kept until gc sees it merged; a check: after finish no lanes/ directory remains under $HARNESS_WORKTREES/proj and the merged lane branches are gone locally and on the bare origin while an unverified one stays on both

cmd_gc: the harness-lane/ prefix joins the harness/ and harness-merge/ passes; slots under lanes/ of an ended run with a dead driver are removed by the worktree pass; --deps covers slots; a check: gc on an ended run with a leftover slot (a killed driver) removes it and stops a stub lane unit harness-<run>-M1-s2.scope, and gc of a run with a live driver touches no slot and no lane unit
names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt (tests/checks/NN-lanes-slots.sh and the gc file); `bash -n bin/harness lib/lane.sh lib/driver.sh`; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: The record PR: finish's last step pushes harness/<run> and opens `<run>: run record` against main, merged under auto, left under pr, skipped under RECORD_PR=off; the end-of-queue gc deletes a merged run's record branch and worktree, never finish itself.
steps: finish, after the retro and the ledger, pushes the record branch and runs `gh pr create --base main --head harness/<run> --title "<run>: run record"` (or reuses the open one) with the report as body; under MERGE_POLICY=auto it runs `gh pr merge --merge` and the PR head is gone with it; under pr the PR is left with `note` saying so; RECORD_PR=off opens none

checks in tests/checks/NN-lanes-record-pr.sh: the record PR's diff in the stub gh's record is only .harness/runs/<run>/ paths; it is opened and merged under auto, left open under pr, absent with off; `harness continue <run>` right after finish still finds harness/<run> on origin (finish deletes nothing)

cmd_gc's record_only keeps its meaning; the queue runner's end-of-queue `gc --all-merged --deps` deletes a merged run's record branch locally and on origin and its record worktree, the ledger keeping the record; a check in the gc file
names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `bash -n lib/driver.sh bin/harness lib/queue.sh`; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: harness status prints one line per open lane, summary.json gains lanes {max_open, lane_hours, wall_hours} with a report.md line, and the initializer and run prompts say how milestones share files and slots.
steps:
`harness status ` prints, for a running run, one line per open lane `lane · · session · port

· slot · `; a check reads it during a held stub run with two lanes open

summary.mjs adds `lanes: {max_open, lane_hours, wall_hours}` (lane hours = the sum of each lane's open-to-close time, from the opened/closed notes or lane state) to summary.json and one line to report.md; the two-lane run of P2-02 has `max_open: 2`; `harness trends` output is unchanged (its check keeps its text)

prompts/initializer.md says milestones that may run side by side should touch different files, shared docs (README.md, docs/architecture.md) are edited in a milestone's closing review feature, and a feature independent of its predecessors in the same milestone gets `after`; prompts/parts/run.md says other lanes of this run work in other slots; a check greps both
names in tests/fixtures/check-names.txt; `node --check lib/summary.mjs`, `bash -n bin/harness`; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing

features.description: An Opus review of the P2 diff from a file: Critical and Important findings fixed RED->GREEN, simplifications applied, decisions and docs complete for two lanes.
steps: `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib bin tests prompts templates docs/architecture.md README.md > /tmp/harness/agent-harness/agent-harness-2026-10-26/P2-review.diff` is read by an Opus subagent; its findings with a severity each are in docs/plans/2026-10-26-P2-review.md
every Critical or Important finding has a check in a tests/checks file that failed before the fix and passes after (the commit messages say which), names added to tests/fixtures/check-names.txt

journal/decisions/2026-10-26-lanes.md covers admission, the re-base rule's place, slots and the record PR; 2026-10-26-parallel-runs-headroom.md and 2026-10-26-lane-rebase-disjoint.md read finding · choice · rejected; none numbers itself D-H<n>

docs/architecture.md §4 names USAGE_5H and the slots; §5 shows admission in the coordinator diagram; §8 the record PR; §12 lanes beside MAX_PARALLEL_RUNS with the headroom rule; §15 updated; README.md names MAX_LANES, LANE_RESERVE_GB, LANE_OPEN_BELOW_5H, LANE_REBASE, RECORD_PR, slots, the record PR, and the after-run steps (MAX_LANES=2, the morning greps); templates/user/config.sh has every lane key commented
`bash -n` on every shell file P2 touched and `node --check` on every .mjs; `bash tests/run.sh` ends with every check passing
